subject: Pricing & batching follow-up — Acme Retail (token volumes & continuous batching)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Huang <ellie.huang@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — token volumes, budget, batching assumptions

Hi Ellie / team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to hear the roadmap for the personalization and recommendations pilots. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put together a tailored quote and compute profile: 

Summary from our call:
- Initial pilot: ~15–25M tokens/month (mainly recommendation prompts + short responses)
- Ramp: targeting ~100–150M tokens/month within 6–12 months if pilot metrics hit OKR thresholds
- Budget range you mentioned: $20k–$30k/month for hosted inference (open to reassign across dedicated/reserved later)
- Target unit economics: you said target ~$25 / 1M tokens (is that target gross spend or net-after-infra?) — want to confirm.

Key technical questions that will materially change the cost/quote:
1) Workload pattern: you mentioned steady traffic with spikes around UX events. Can you confirm approximate QPS or concurrency during peak?
2) Batching expectations: is the workload tolerant of small batching windows (continuous batching — i.e., slight micro-queueing to improve throughput) or do you need strict <200ms p95 latency for all requests?
3) Long-context jobs: what percent of requests are long-context (>=512–2048 token outputs)? You mentioned a smaller set of summary jobs — ballpark percent would help (e.g., 10% vs 40%).

Attached: redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx (pricing bands + example cost models) and a draft SOW for pilot (SOW-draft-Acme-2026-05.pdf).

If you can confirm the three items above, I’ll get Marissa to run a cost projection under continuous batching vs strict low-latency profiles and share a recommended configuration (model variant, quantization profile, expected $/1M tokens with caching/batching).

Would you be open to a short 30-minute follow-up next week to review the numbers? Proposed times: Tue 9–11am PT or Wed 1–3pm PT.

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes

camila.reyes@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0189

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — token volumes, budget, batching assumptions

Camila — thanks for the note and for the helpful deck. Confirming the numbers from our side: 

- Pilot month 1–3: expect 20M tokens/month (we under-forecast a little on purpose)
- Ramp months 4–12: 80–150M tokens/month depending on rollout speed and personalization adoption
- Budget: comfortable with a $20k–$30k/month committed spend for hosted inference during pilot. We'll consider a Dedicated/reserved capex commit if unit economics justify it.

Unit economics / target: when I said ~$25 / 1M tokens, I meant net spend (what we pay you) — ideally we target <= $30 / 1M tokens for now. If there are caching or batching levers that bring this down to ~$15–20 / 1M tokens, that would be compelling and justify a reserved arrangement.

Workload characteristics:
- Traffic profile: relatively steady during business hours with predictable spikes for marketing campaigns (~1.5–2x baseline).
- Short prompts (~<=100 tokens): ~60% of calls (recommendation + quick context)
- Long jobs (summaries, long-context enrichments, ~512–1024 output tokens): ~40% of calls
- Concurrency/peak: baseline ~120 concurrent requests across regions, peak ~350 concurrent during promos — we can provide more precise telemetry if it helps.

Latency tolerance: for recommendations we want p95 <= 400ms ideally; for long summaries p95 <= 1.5s is acceptable. We can tolerate small batching windows (20–50ms) if it materially improves cost.

Next steps: please send a cost projection with two profiles — (A) lowest-latency (p95 <=400ms) pricing and (B) continuous-batching optimized (allow 20–50ms queue, caching enabled) pricing — plus recommended model variants. Also cc procurement for any contract redlines.

Thanks — happy to take the 30m follow-up Tue 9:30am PT.
Ellie
Ellie Huang
Director, ML Platform — Acme Retail
ellie.huang@acme-retail.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Huang <ellie.huang@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — token volumes, budget, batching assumptions

Thanks Ellie — super helpful and clear. Quick notes inline + what we will produce before Tue 9:30am PT: 

- Confirmed: pilot 20M/month, ramp to 80–150M/month. Budget constraint acknowledged ($20–30k/mo).
- Unit economics: we’ll show modeled $/1M tokens for both hosted and dedicated scenarios. Our baseline projections typically assume: no caching, per-token runtime cost X; with continuous batching + prefix/KV caching we often see 30–60% reduction in effective per-token spend for workloads with repeated prefixes (your recommender use case looks like a good fit).

On batching / latency tradeoffs:
- Continuous batching (what we refer to internally as micro-batching) collects requests for a short window (e.g., 10–50ms) and runs a larger efficient kernel that increases throughput and reduces GPU utilization. Benefits: lower $/1M tokens and more predictable warm KV cache utilization. Cost: adds a small queuing latency (20–50ms typical) and can increase p95 by ~30–200ms depending on traffic variability.
- For your profile (60% short, 40% long): continuous batching + KV cache will likely move unit cost toward the lower end of your target — our initial model will show an example: hosted (A100 class) running medium-size model => projected $20–$28 / 1M tokens for low-latency profile, and ~$12–$18 / 1M tokens with continuous batching + caching. We’ll provide the exact math in the spreadsheet.

Questions to finalize the model:
1) Do you have a breakdown of percentage of requests that are cacheable (i.e., identical prefixes across users)? Even a rough estimate (e.g., 25% cacheable) helps.
2) Are summaries tolerant of slightly higher tail latency (1.5s p95 you mentioned suggests yes — we can batch more aggressively there).

Deliverables before Tue call:
- Two cost profiles (low-latency vs batching-optimized) with $/1M tokens and expected monthly spend at 20M and 100M tokens.
- Suggested model/config (model size, quantization level, expected GPU class).
- Proposed SLOs and recommended routing policy (e.g., route recommendations to low-latency pool, summaries to batching pool).

I’ll ask Marissa to prepare the cost models and Aditya to sketch the routing/batching config. See you Tue 9:30am PT.

Best,
Camila

Camila / team / Ellie — adding the attachments and next steps. I ran a quick high-level cost model and attached an initial pricing worksheet (redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx). Highlights: 

- Low-latency profile (p95 <=400ms): estimated $/1M tokens = $24–$30 depending on model selection (13B vs 30B family); monthly spend at 20M = ~$480–$600; at 100M = ~$2.4k–$3.0k (note these are runtime-only numbers; we'll add platform fees in final quote).
- Continuous-batching + caching (20–50ms queue acceptable): estimated $/1M tokens = $11–$18 depending on cache hit rate and model variant. With a 30% cache hit, 100M effective tokens could look like $12–$15 / 1M.

Next steps: I’ll finalize a formal quote and tailored SOW. Camila — will you confirm if we should include a Dedicated capacity option (1-year commit) in the deck? Ellie / procurement — if you’re open, we can include a committed Reserved option in parallel so you can compare.

Proposed follow-up: Tue 9:30am PT (Camila / Ellie) to review the attached.

Marissa Cole
